item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Sold Over 53 Million Units and Grossed $4.7 Billion in Its First Week, According to Alinea Analytics Estimates
item.description:
A full week has passed since the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI , and Alinea Analytics is back with updated sales estimates, following their initial report on the massive debut weekend .

According to the analyst firm, Rockstar's latest masterpiece has already sold over 53 million units , generating $4.7 billion in gross revenue. The list of astounding figures goes on: almost 7 million players have already spent over 50 hours in Leonida, and 250K of them have surpassed the 100-hour mark. US players represent 33.5% of all GTA VI purchases on PlayStation 5; moreover, the split between PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S|X is actually widening, with Microsoft's share shrinking to 24.3% (it started at 25.8%) of the total.

Next, the Alinea Analytics report examines the commercial performance of 11 recent AAA games before and during the launch week of Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5. The games are 007 First Light, Phantom Blade Zero, Wolverine, Crimson Desert, The Blood of Dawnwalker, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced, Ghost of Yotei, Star Wars Galactic Racer, Onimusha Way of the Sword, Resident Evil Requiem, and Gran Turismo 7.

Unsurprisingly, revenue fell sharply by 24% across these games from November 19 to 25. The worst case is Phantom Blade Zero, which launched last month to great reviews and initial success but saw its PS5 sales halve each week , including this past week. Even setting PBZ aside, though, the rest of the titles still registered a 12% revenue drop, as shown in the slide below.

There are three outliers, though:

  • Polyphony's Gran Turismo 7 nearly doubled its full-price sales, with unit sales rising 96% and revenue climbing 86% (from $1.0M to $1.9M).
  • Sucker Punch's Ghost of Yotei , also sold at full price during the week, saw revenue rise 31% , from $542K to $710K, and copies sold increased 34% . Granted, it had the boost of the Complete Edition and Echoes of Sekigahara DLC that launched last month .
  • CAPCOM's Resident Evil Requiem remained priced at $55.99, the same as the previous week. Revenue grew 13%, from $751K to $846K, while copies sold rose 15%.

Overall, Grand Theft Auto VI's groundbreaking debut clearly had a major impact on unit sales and revenue on the PlayStation 5 premium game market , but some of the biggest titles released over the past year were resilient enough to hold their momentum.

item.title: Elon Musk Brands Rival Cloud Giants “Slowpokes” and “Hyposcalers” While Saying Google Could Join Anthropic in Renting More Compute from SpaceX
item.description:
Over the past few days, Elon Musk has repeatedly claimed that Anthropic is eyeing more compute from SpaceX — a projection directly challenged by a recent note from SemiAnalysis's institutional desk.

Now, Musk is doubling down. The SpaceX chief says Google is also looking to expand the compute it rents from the company, while dismissing rival hyperscalers as "slowpokes" who would be better described as "hyposcalers."

Despite a purported pushback from SemiAnalysis over his Anthropic claims, Elon Musk doubles down — claiming Google wants in too while branding SpaceX's rival cloud giants "hyposcalers."

Earlier in November, we reported on a recent meeting between Anthropic's executives and sell-side analysts, where the former bluntly stated that the AI lab's compute deal with SpaceX would not be extended beyond the middle of next year , or Q2 2027.

Those reports then prompted a fairly blasé response from Elon Musk, who said SpaceX "would be happy to take the compute back," while adding that "the opposite is going to happen."

Musk then went a step further a few days later , declaring:

"When I’ve talked to Anthropic, they tell me it is extremely likely that they will continue to rent compute from SpaceX, and in fact, that they want significantly more."

The next twist in this saga came earlier this week, when a note from SemiAnalysis's institutional desk revealed that Anthropic might not renew its contract with SpaceX for a cluster of around 50,000 H200 GPUs.

That is a significant stake: SpaceX earned nearly a third of its revenue from Anthropic in Q3 2026. Starting in December 2026, Anthropic is slated to pay SpaceX $3.1 billion per month once all contracted compute is delivered — though the deal becomes cancelable after early 2027 with 90 days' notice

The note also asserted that SpaceX has already begun offering this compute capacity to other customers, with availability expected as soon as early 2027 and a quoted price of about $5 per GPU-hour.

Meanwhile, SpaceX has also reportedly slashed its Blackwell GPU spot quote for small compute clusters from about $15.0–$15.5 per GPU-hour to $10–$12, aligning these rates with its quotes for large-scale clusters already serving major customers such as Anthropic and Google.

Now, however, Elon Musk has weighed in — responding to an X post speculating on Anthropic and Google's future compute demand by noting :

"Not sure who will buy more, but Google has expressed interest in renting more compute from us."

For context, Google is currently paying SpaceX $920 million per month to rent its compute in a deal that runs through June 2029.

Musk also clarified why SpaceX reduced its Blackwell GPU spot quote for some customers, noting that while large blocks of compute still command a hefty premium, the rental price of small clusters has dropped:

"The rental price for large, coherent blocks of compute configured for high-bandwidth training is increasing, sometimes very significantly, but the price for small amounts of compute (below ~5k GPUs) is decreasing."

"Overall, the average rental price per GPU for SpaceX compute is rising."

Elsewhere, Elon Musk took pointed jabs at SpaceX's hyperscale rivals , calling them "hyposcalers" and "slowpokes":

"People have no idea what happens when a super capable hardware company enters an arena of slowpokes."

"Hyposcalers would be a more accurate description."

As a refresher, SpaceX plans to end 2026 with 2.5–3 GW of compute capacity and add roughly 10 GW in 2027 to reach around 13 GW — while its broader power and cooling footprint targets up to 20 GW. To fund this expansion, SpaceX's 2027 compute-related CapEx alone is expected to surge to $390 billion (about $30 billion per GW).

item.title: Windows Update Is Still Pushing A Vulnerable Intel Driver That Microsoft’s Own Defender Flags As A Security Threat
item.description:
In yet another rather ironic episode involving Windows 11 , Microsoft is reportedly continuing to distribute an outdated Intel driver through Windows Update , despite its own antivirus software, Microsoft Defender, identifying an associated component as a legitimate security threat. Even removing the offending driver apparently doesn't stop Windows Update from offering it again .

Windows Update Continues To Offer A Nearly Four-Year-Old Intel Driver Containing A Component With A Known Security Vulnerability Dating Back To 2020

As uncovered by German publication Deskmodder , Microsoft Defender recently flagged a file named OpenHardwareMonitorLib.sys on an 11th-generation Intel NUC system , classifying it as VulnerableDriver:WinNT/Winring0 , with a severe threat rating.

The file was traced back to Intel's Performance Driver Extension (version 1.0.0.38) , a component of the Intel NUC Software Studio Service dating back to December 8, 2022 .

After disabling the associated service and removing the driver package from the Windows Driver Store, the publication queried the Windows Update Agent API , only to discover that Microsoft was still offering the exact same driver version for download .

Further examination revealed that the package contains WinRing0 components embedded within a digitally signed DLL . Interestingly, scanning the downloaded package with Microsoft Defender did not produce any security warnings , potentially because the flagged driver is only extracted at runtime. The publication did not reinstall the package to conclusively verify this behavior.

For those unfamiliar, WinRing0 provides low-level hardware access to applications, including utilities that monitor temperatures, voltages, and other hardware parameters . However, a security vulnerability documented under CVE-2020-14979 can allow attackers to elevate their privileges on an already-accessible system .

Microsoft itself explicitly acknowledges that the detection is legitimate, rather than a false positive. This does not, however, necessarily indicate that an affected PC has been compromised .

Intel Has Known About The Issue Since At Least August 2025, And Even Recommends Discontinuing Use Of The Software

Perhaps the most concerning aspect of this discovery is that the issue is hardly new. An Intel Community forum thread from August 2025 describes virtually the same behavior, with users reporting recurring Defender warnings after Windows Update reinstalled the problematic driver.

An Intel customer support representative subsequently acknowledged the WinRing0 detections, explaining that NUC Software Studio had reached the end of its security support lifecycle.

In fact, Intel had already published a security advisory in December 2024 concerning separate vulnerabilities affecting the software, recommending that users uninstall or discontinue its use.

The discovery also comes at a particularly awkward time for Microsoft, which has been promoting its Driver Quality Initiative alongside ongoing efforts to remove obsolete drivers from Windows Update to improve security and reliability.

While Intel's discontinued software is undoubtedly part of the problem, one would expect Microsoft's own security and update infrastructures to be better coordinated. After all, users shouldn't have to fight Windows Update to keep a driver that Microsoft's own antivirus considers vulnerable off their systems.

News Sources: Deskmodder , Clubic , Microsoft Support , Intel Security Advisory , Intel Community

Intel's bLLC is expected to serve as the company's answer to AMD's 3D V-Cache technology, which helps immensely in improving gaming performance. We already know that Nova Lake-S bLLC variants aim to deliver such a gaming performance boost, and according to the recent leaks, some chips could deliver up to 20% better gaming performance than Arrow Lake-S.

item.title: AI Bloatware Arrives On Windows 11; Lenovo Is Shipping Select Business Laptops With ChatGPT Pre-Installed, With Businesses Getting A $100 Incentive
item.description:
Laptop manufacturers were already trigger-happy shipping a boatload of machines with a ton of bloatware that would require ample time to remove. Even now, a fresh copy of Windows 11 arrives with a plethora of unwanted software, and it appears that the situation will worsen with time.

Lenovo, the world’s largest PC manufacturer, has reportedly begun pre-installing the desktop version of ChatGPT on select new Windows 11 business notebooks, signaling a new wave of third-party AI software bundling on commercial hardware. To make the offer salivating for business operators, an OpenAI promotion offers corporate buyers up to $100 per seat in workspace credits.

The proliferation of ChatGPT running on business laptops has begun, as business owners will gladly accept OpenAI’s $100 credit and potentially save millions

Details uncovered in an OpenAI support document by Windows Latest confirm that the promotional credits are strictly tied to eligible Lenovo devices that ship with ChatGPT pre-installed from the factory. Businesses with an existing ChatGPT Business workspace can claim a one-time $100 credit toward their shared workspace balance simply by signing in through the pre-installed client.

Companies that create a new Business workspace through the offer will reportedly receive a substantially larger incentive. However, as you’d expect, the promotion arrives with certain hurdles. For instance, you can avail two credit tiers, as the funds are deposited into the workspace’s shared balance with a 60-day expiration window.

It should also be mentioned that the offer can only be availed through the pre-installed ChatGPT app. OpenAI says to “Look for ChatGPT in Start. You may also see it in Lenovo Now or Lenovo Vantage. Contact Lenovo if you’re unsure whether ChatGPT came preinstalled on your device.”

Lenovo is following the same approach as Microsoft, with the latter bundling Copilot natively into Windows 11. The Chinese PC manufacturer will soon expand its AI partnership across consumer product lines such as Yoga and Legion, meaning one additional program that users have to uninstall if they prefer using competitors’ solutions such as Claude or Gemini. In any case, if businesses are willing to save millions over these $100 credits, then there’s no question that AI bloatware will be prevalent in even more laptop brands.

Assuming more of these programs will start being bundled with Lenovo’s laptops, the company should at least take a back seat in pre-installing its other bloatware, as it consumes unnecessary storage and resources. There’s also a possibility that these unwanted programs could be wearing down the SSD when running as background tasks, but there’s no way to confirm this behavior, at least for now.

The role of AI has branched out towards diagnosing software-related issues, with the latest case centering around GIGABYTE. According to the latest report, the company allegedly dismissed its entire Control Center development team following widespread complaints that its RGB lighting utility causes persistent frame-pacing stutters on NVIDIA graphics cards. According to a report originating from Brazil, the root cause of the performance degradation was uncovered by an independent researcher using AI-assisted reverse engineering.

RGB polling causes GPU performance drops, emphasizing the need for these companies to pour more resources into optimizing their software

If you’ve ever been a victim of half-baked software from companies like GIGABYTE, ASUS, MSI, or others, you’re not alone, and there are countless accounts on Reddit that have criticized these firms, yet somehow, even after all these years, there isn’t a solution. Fortunately, as TudoCelular reports, an independent researcher spent roughly a month investigating recurring stutters caused by GIGABYTE’s software.

Through AI-assisted analysis and reverse engineering, the researcher traced the bottleneck directly to how GIGABYTE Control Center’s RGB module communicates with NVIDIA GPUs and onboard lighting controllers, which ended up interfering with NVIDIA’s display drivers. While GIGABYTE has not officially confirmed any layoffs or restructuring within its software division, hardware enthusiasts across Reddit and PC building forums have extensively documented the stuttering behavior.

Complaints have been prominent among users running RTX 50-series GPUs, including AORUS RTX 5080 and RTX 5090 models, alongside X870 motherboards. To address the instability, a new version of GIGABYTE Control Center was pushed on November 26, aimed at improving software stability and resolving NVIDIA compatibility conflicts. For users who continue to experience frame-time spikes after updating, GIGABYTE recommends switching the RGB lighting effects to a static mode to reduce background polling overhead.

Alternatively, PC builders should look to eliminate vendor background services altogether, or leverage the use of open-source tools like OpenRGB. Of course, we cannot reiterate enough how these companies should inject additional resources so that the lack of software optimization doesn’t interfere with a user’s gaming experience.

item.title: SpaceX’s One Million Data Center Satellites Got FCC Approval, But Plans To Park Unneeded Satellites Around The Sun Are On Hold
item.description:
SpaceX's recent win at the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which saw the regulator grant the firm approval to launch a million data center satellites in space, came with a caveat. As part of its application, SpaceX had asked the Commission to also allow it to dispose of unneeded satellites by placing them in heliocentric disposal orbits or disposal orbits around Earth. However, the FCC deferred the request as it remarked that SpaceX's proposal did not highlight whether the disposals would comply with regulatory requirements.

SpaceX Must Justify Non-Atmospheric Disposal Of Data Center Satellites Prior To Deployment, Says FCC

The data center satellites, which SpaceX refers to as the Starmind constellation, will operate in four groups ranging from 686 kilometers to 1,002 kilometers in orbit, according to the firm's filings. The precise number of satellites sits at 998,240, and SpaceX will rely on its experience with the Starlink satellite internet constellation to ensure that the spacecraft are sustainable users of space.

On this front, the firm's original FCC filing indicated that it would either dispose of the satellites through atmospheric re-entry or "by placing them into disposal orbits around Earth or into heliocentric disposal orbits." Currently, SpaceX's Starlink satellites rely on atmospheric re-entry for disposal as the spacecraft burn up before impacting the ground, and the new plan would involve heliocentric orbits - orbits measured from the Sun's center.

After the FCC asked SpaceX for additional information regarding its non-atmospheric satellite disposal plans, the firm provided additional details in a submission on May 29th. It shared that while all satellites operating below 600 kilometers would be disposed of through atmospheric re-entry, it would "tailor disposal plans to the specific orbital parameters and mission profiles of the satellites."

Crucially, while seeking a waiver of the FCC's rule which requires atmospheric disposal, SpaceX shared that:

"SpaceX conducted hypervelocity testing confirming that impacts to the Starlink solar array design result in minimal debris generation. The arrays consist primarily of lightweight, flexible thin-film photovoltaic materials and supporting substrates that would likely fragment into negligible pieces upon impact. In contrast, the satellite bus contains dense structural components, electronics, batteries, and propulsion elements whose disruption would be far more likely to produce debris capable of creating secondary collision risks."

However, the Commission appeared unsatisfied, as in its authorizing order for the Starmind data center satellite internet constellation, it noted :

"Because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements, SpaceX’s waiver request is deferred. Prior to deploying and operating any Starmind satellites that will not be disposed of via atmospheric re-entry, SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules."

The Starmind satellites are integral to SpaceX's business plans, following the firm's pivot to becoming an artificial intelligence compute provider. While its SEC filings earlier this year estimated a $28.5 trillion total addressable market from AI, Elon Musk believes the actual figure could be higher .

item.title: Warframe Creative Director Rebecca Ford Calls Tau “The Biggest Swing We Could Do”, but Says December 9 Is Only the Start
item.description:
Canadian developer Digital Extremes has finally given a date for Warframe: Tau , an update players have waited years for. It's the game's first trip beyond its original star system, launching simultaneously on December 9 for free on PC, console, and mobile. Ahead of the Devstream, Community Director Megan Everett and Creative Director Rebecca Ford gave the press a preview from a work-in-progress dev build, followed by a roundtable Q&A. Below is a summary of the presentation and Q&A.

The Presentation

Tau has been mentioned in Warframe's lore for years and teased more heavily over the last five, most notably during the pivotal Tau conversation in The New War . Ford described it as " the biggest swing we could do " for the game, but stressed that December 9 is only the start. At launch, Tau includes two regions, a roughly two-hour quest, new syndicates, and a full album of music. It also arrives immediately after the Epoch Operation: Taubound , which ended with the Infested home world Eris being consumed. Everett noted that Taubound was the most participated-in event in Warframe's history. The Infested will get their response in 2027, when the developer plans an Infested-focused deep dive in the Origin System.

The first Heirloom of 2027, Nezha , will be bundled with a Loki Heirloom. Loki, one of the starter Warframes from the alpha days, will also get a light rework covering synergies within his kit and the role of invisibility and crowd control; full details will be shared in an upcoming official Devstream. The Loki Heirloom includes an optional cloak that uses a new fur shader, part of the tech that the game shares with Soulframe .

Kullervo Prime launches with Tau as its Prime Access, revealed through a combined Prime trailer that also features Styanax. Ford said it had taken six months to go from idea to execution. Kullervo Prime gets increased armor and energy and arrives with two new Prime weapons , the Rauta Prime shotgun and the Vitrica Prime heavy blade. It can be earned for free through gameplay or unlocked instantly with a microtransaction.

A new navigation screen lets players choose between the Origin System and Tau. The first of the two available regions, Parita , will be familiar to players who know Warframe's quests and lore. It's an environmentally volatile desert region hit by sandstorms and home to descendants of the Dax . It features six game modes, including a version of Survival with environmental hazards and an ecological system in which players hunt for larvae and bugs on behalf of Catylac, a young boy focused on science.

Arguably, though, the headline region is Fornax , a ringed Sentient city with a noir, mob-run casino theme (and its own weather system, which, of course, includes rain) and Warframe's first interconnected social hub system. It has three connected hubs :

  • the Last Bloom Lounge, which is the casino;
  • the Manifold;
  • a third hub that is still kept under wraps.

Players can travel between the hubs in four ways:

  • running bounties from one hub to the next, starting with the bounty giver Larynde;
  • launching missions from the star chart;
  • driving along the Highway Network, a car combat mini-game played from each hub's garage, where mob cars chase you down along Sentient highways for resources;
  • taking a Night Walk, a first-person, non-combat mode in which you walk Brisco's hound to a destination of your choosing, picking up resources and clues along the way.

Spy returns after a long absence as a vault heist, in which players memorize codes and passwords to break into vaults. Mayhem is a brand-new mode in which you destroy the mob's property, including blowing up its limousines. The press release also lists Racket , where squads recover stolen funds and return them to extorted neighborhoods, and says Fornax offers four remixed versions of existing mission types in total. Tau also introduces new combinable damage types.

Acolytes can't follow players to Tau. Instead, the mob sends the five Hokra Brothers after anyone playing Steel Path missions. Each brother has variants and a personality of his own, and players can meet them off-duty in the casino hub. Steel Essence farming is shared with the Origin System , so it won't become a separate grind, which I'm sure players will be pleased with.

Instead of three separate syndicates, all of Fornax progresses through a single one, The Fornax Informer , a trio of newsies who know and publish everything happening in the city. At rank three, players can start detective work : collecting clues to solve a scandal at the Last Bloom Lounge and earn an exclusive reward. Fornax also has its own skill progression system , with buffs that apply in Fornax missions and unlock by completing challenges.

Fornax also introduces Warframe's first card game , which can be played against the house, against other players, or with a squad. During the demo, Everett won her hand on a final draw. The casino has a lounge singer, and Larynde is accompanied by a Sentient microphone with its own store. Tau's soundtrack is a full album that Ford described as "EDM meets trip hop meets acid wash".

Digital Extremes also proudly noted that Warframe, which now has more than 90 million players , is nominated for Best Community Support at The Game Awards. Watching Geoff Keighley's show on December 10 for 30 minutes with a linked Twitch account earns players a free Caliban.

The Q&A

After the press demo, Everett and Ford added several details about Tau's launch content and DE's plans for 2027 during the subsequent Q&A.

First of all, the studio expects Tau's quest to take roughly two hours , depending on how much time players spend on optional moments. Parita's working codename was " Mad Max Dax ," and the developers called the Mad Max worldview, with its deserts, sandstorms and tribal regression of humanity, the region's main inspiration. Fornax came from a 2023 idea: Digital Extremes wished the return to the Sentients to feel like a cyber Detroit crossed with Atlantic City, and said its sci-fi elements are the furthest Warframe has ever gone. Mass Effect was also cited as a major influence, down to Brisco's design, along with Law & Order (Brisco is named after Lenny Briscoe ), The Sopranos and Boardwalk Empire . The team said the Sentients are the hardest faction to write for in Warframe, and that framing them through crime, mafia, gambling and addiction is what finally made them work.

Brisco is a Chimera frame, a status the quest explains through the Entrati's involvement. The developers will only make more Chimeras for bespoke, character-driven moments, and no others are in development. However, players will meet a new Tau Warframe next year.

The choice of mission types was described as a sliding scale . At one end are brand-new, high-flavor modes like Mayhem. At the other is Survival, which is always the most played mode because it's comfortable and players rarely fail it. Spy was brought back because it had gone untouched for years and suits builds like Ivara's.

The Hokra Brothers are meant to be somewhat longer fights than Acolytes, though DE expects the community's builds to deal with them anyway. Stalker and the other existing hunters won't appear in Tau; if they do, it's a bug.

In Tau's endless missions, enemy levels rise at a rate similar to Void Cascade, so players reach level cap faster. DE might apply the same rate to the Origin System. Tau launches with just three new weapons. The new combinable damage types will let the physical types (Slash, Puncture and Impact) combine with Tau damage, much as elemental damage types already combine.

Fornax has more open spaces , and the developers insisted on one non-negotiable rule: if you fall off the level, you die. With new grappling hooks and Warframe abilities in play, the developers think the risk of falling changes how players move through levels. They said they wish they'd introduced it earlier, but it's too late to retrofit to the Origin System .

Fornax's skill progression is permanent , and players can swap which skills are active. The Highway Network car is a creature, not a moddable vehicle, and the driving is a low-stakes mini-game. The Night Walk exists for players who have long wanted to explore Warframe’s open worlds without being shot at .

A roulette game is coming early next year to join the card game. Everett and Ford also hinted that more of the Tau system will arrive sooner than players might expect. Floofs (Warframe's plush collectibles) based on the newsies or the Hokra Brothers may follow, depending on player demand.

Looking ahead, the pair described 2027 as a year focused on the Infested in the Origin System , a faction it believes has never been explored in real depth in the game’s long live service history. It compared the approach to 1999 : going all in on one storyline, then bringing the threads back together.

DE also acknowledged a growing problem with paying off old storylines. Story points still feel fresh to the team, but The New War is now five years old for players, so future quests will need to do more to remind players of past events. There won't be a spoiler recap before Tau; the developers will instead lean on its official content creators and the solar system intro shown at TennoCon.

Everett and Ford called returning players Warframe’s biggest " white whale ." Someone who quit years ago comes back exactly where they left off, often facing the same grind that drove them away. The team hopes to focus on returning players in 2027 , including systemic fixes to the login experience.

When asked what they're most excited about, the developers pointed to a specific moment in the Tau quest that they believe resets the story around fundamentals and sets a clear direction for its characters and conflict. They also singled out the music, the new weather system, and the scale of the undertaking: building a second star system took everything the team has learned over 13 years , and work on the December 9 build is still ongoing.

item.title: Not Just NVIDIA’s Drivers, But Razer’s Audio Utility Is Also Wearing Down SSDs; One User Shows 3.2GB Of I/O Write Bytes Recorded In Less Than Two Hours
item.description:
NVIDIA has recently been under fire for pushing out Game Ready GPU driver updates without realizing that versions 621.14 and 621.24 were excessively writing to SSDs , wearing them down in a short time span. Even though the company has seemingly resolved the matter with version 621.40 , these display drivers aren’t the only software afflicting your pricey solid-state drives. One user reveals that Razer’s standalone 7.1 Surround Sound utility also continuously writes data to the host drive.

The background process “rzappengine.exe” found by one user was revealed to be continuously writing data to the SSD; playing audio increases the write rate

The issue came to light after Redditor “u/Stefouch” installed the standalone Razer 7.1 Surround Sound software for a newly acquired BlackShark V3 X Hyperspeed headset without installing the full Razer Synapse 4 suite. After inspecting system activity through Sysinternals Process Explorer and Windows Resource Monitor, it was found that the utility rapidly accumulates gigabytes of I/O write operations, continuously writing data to the host drive at speeds between 0.6MB/s and 1MB/s, regardless of whether the application is logged in or sitting idle.

“As soon as the executable starts, it writes non-stop at ~640 kB/s. If I start playing audio through it, it increases up to 1 MB/s and won’t decrease until I restart the app. In just a few minutes, it reaches a gigabyte of total I/O writes.”

In the image below, you can clearly spot that the rzappengine.exe background process has accumulated 3.2GB of “I/O Write Bytes” in just a couple of hours. Even though the Redditor didn’t mention the time his system was operational, he does state that the process reaches 1GB of total I/O writes in just a few minutes when writing at 640KB/s when idle and up to 1MB/s during audio playback. If you do the math, that 3.2GB accumulation can take between 55 and 85 minutes of runtime, or just under an hour and a half.

In response to the Reddit thread, another user commented that aggressive disk logging has long been a characteristic of Razer’s background software ecosystem, warning that simply blocking write permissions to the log directory will break application functionality. Fortunately, there’s a remedy to this, which is redirecting the local Razer AppData folder to a secondary drive or a volatile RAM drive using a Windows directory junction. While it’s not the best of solutions out there, the only other alternative is that the Redditor stops firing up Razer’s 7.1 Surround Sound software.

News Source: Reddit

item.description:
Amidst the ongoing AI wave and booming memory chip prices, workers at memory chip giant SK hynix are set to receive massive bonuses once again. Details gathered by ChosunBiz show that in the third quarter, SK hynix accrued 230 million Korean won ($170,000 at an exchange rate of 1 won = $1,333) in bonuses per employee, which are slated to be paid next year. Overall, if the firm meets its annually profit targets, then its bonus per employee could cross $550,000 or $4.5 trillion.

SK hynix's Profit Sharing Bonus To Be Split 50/50 In Cash & Share Payments

Reports of SK hynix employees receiving massive bonuses made rounds earlier this year when it was revealed that the firm could end up paying roughy $2.5 billion in bonuses just in the first quarter of 2026. Then, in August, reports claimed that the bonuses would be paid 40% in cash and 60% in stock for the performance-based bonus program.

Now, ChosunBiz shares that for the third quarter, SK hynix's total profit-sharing bonuses, which account for 10% of the firm's operating profits, sit at 8.3 trillion won or $622 billion. Dividing the figure by the firm's employee count of 36,`50 leads to a figure of 230 million won per employee or roughly $170,000.

The firm's bonus program is divided into two portions based on productivity and on profit. The productivity bonus can be as high as 150% of the employee's monthly base pay depending on the firm's profit margins. The performance bonus is tied to the operating profit, with employees receiving 10% of SK hynix's operating profit as a bonus, with management recently having removed a cap that limited this bonus to 1,000% of the base pay.

For the performance bonus, SK hynix is slated to pay 80% of this year's bonus early next year. 50% of the bonus will be paid in cash, while 30% will be paid in stock. Additionally, the remaining 20% will be paid in two installments over the next couple of years.

The booming demand for memory chips has also shaken up Korea's industry. SK hynix and peer Samsung are reportedly struggling to find labor for their massive chip manufacturing projects. SK hynix's bonuses have also led to turmoil at Samsung, whose employees threatened a strike earlier this year to negotiate similar payments for themselves. Employees had demanded 15% of operating profit as a bonus, and the strike was estimated by analysts to cost as much as $11.7 billion to Samsung.

item.title: This PCIe 5.0 Expansion Card Turns A Single x16 Slot Into Four GPU Connections, Opening Up New Possibilities For Local AI Rigs
item.description:
Building a multi-GPU workstation for local AI workloads doesn't necessarily have to involve an expensive server-grade motherboard. An intriguing PCIe 5.0 expansion card making the rounds on social media allows users to connect up to four graphics cards through a single PCIe x16 slot , without requiring motherboard-level PCIe bifurcation .

Broadcom-Powered PCIe 5.0 Expansion Card Supports Four GPUs At Gen5 x8, Two GPUs At Gen5 x16, Or Eight NVMe SSDs

Highlighted by Caveman Tech on X , the expansion card in question is LR-LINK's LRSV9500-4I , which leverages Broadcom's PEX89048 , a 48-lane PCIe 5.0 switch featuring a rated latency of just 115 nanoseconds .

Of those 48 lanes, 16 are allocated to the upstream connectio n to the host system, while the remaining 32 are distributed among connected devices through four Mini Cool Edge ( MCIO) 8i connectors.

According to the manufacturer , the card supports three configurations:

  • 4 × PCIe 5.0 x8: Four graphics cards.
  • 2 × PCIe 5.0 x16: Two graphics cards.
  • 8 × PCIe 5.0 x4: Eight NVMe SSDs.

Unlike conventional passive PCIe expansion adapters, the onboard switch handles lane distribution independently, eliminating the need for motherboard-level bifurcation support .

Furthermore, thanks to PCIe 5.0 doubling the bandwidth per lane over its predecessor, each Gen5 x8 connection offers roughly 32 GB/s of theoretical bandwidth in each direction, equivalent to a full PCIe 4.0 x16 connection .

That makes the card particularly interesting for owners of NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs looking to build multi-GPU systems for running large language models locally.

We've previously covered MCIO-based external GPU solutions , but this particular implementation takes things a step further by accommodating multiple GPUs through a single host connection.

A Promising Solution For Local AI Enthusiasts, But Its $1,100+ Price Tag And P2P Limitations Are Worth Considering

Naturally, there's a catch. All connected devices share the same PCIe 5.0 x16 upstream link , limiting their combined bandwidth to the host to approximately 64 GB/s in each direction .

While this may be less problematic for certain inference workloads where model weights remain resident in VRAM, communication-intensive workloads, including some tensor-parallel inference configurations and AI training, could encounter bottlenecks.

The switch also doesn't magically enable direct peer-to-peer (P2P) communication on consumer graphics cards where driver-level restrictions prevent it, as Caveman Tech clarified in the replies to his original post.

Pricing is another consideration. The expansion card can be found on AliExpress , while LR-LINK's official storefront lists it at $1,129 , with various GPU and SSD expansion configurations available.

Cheaper PCIe 4.0 switch-based alternatives may consequently make more financial sense for owners of older graphics cards.

Nevertheless, with local AI enthusiasts increasingly looking to overcome the VRAM limitations of individual consumer GPUs, hardware like this could provide an interesting alternative to traditional workstation platforms, provided the necessary cabling, power delivery, cooling, and software support are in place.

News Source: Caveman Tech (X) , LR-LINK , Broadcom

item.title: Chinese Researchers Develop Ray Tracing Algorithm That Delivers Up To 59% Faster Rendering With Less Than 1% Additional Memory Usage
item.description:
As real-time ray tracing and path tracing continue to push modern gaming hardware to its limits, researchers are exploring increasingly clever ways to reduce their computational overhead without relying exclusively on more powerful hardware.

Researchers at China's Wuhan University have developed a promising ray tracing optimization algorithm dubbed BMA (Bounding-Volume Mapping Heuristic Mapping Algorithm) , which achieves up to 1.59x faster rendering while maintaining high image quality and introducing negligible memory overhead .

BMA Accelerates Ray Tracing By Intelligently Skipping Redundant BVH Traversal Operations

Modern ray tracing implementations rely on Bounding Volume Hierarchies (BVHs) , tree-like acceleration structures that allow rays to efficiently locate potentially intersecting geometry without individually testing every triangle within a scene.

However, repeatedly traversing these structures remains computationally expensive, particularly when simulating multiple light bounces in path-traced environments.

Detailed in a research paper published in Computers , BMA exploits the spatial coherence of rays originating from neighboring pixels. It samples representative rays across image tiles, estimates their likely traversal paths, and uses these predictions to let subsequent rays begin traversal deeper within the BVH .

Essentially, the algorithm allows rays to take computational shortcuts rather than repeatedly navigating the same branches of an acceleration structure .

The researchers evaluated BMA against an unmodified implementation of Intel's open-source Embree ray tracing library , rendering 100 frames at 1080p with a maximum path length of five .

The Sponza benchmark demonstrated particularly impressive results, with approximately 48% fewer BVH traversal operations and a 37% reduction in rendering time.

Meanwhile, additional memory consumption remained below 1% across all tested scenes.

BMA Could Complement Existing Ray Tracing Optimizations, But There Are Some Caveats

Unlike conventional, mathematically exact traversal optimizations, BMA trades a small degree of rendering accuracy for improved performance . Nevertheless, all tested scenes achieved PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) values exceeding 35 dB and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index Measure) scores above 0.90 .

Visual inaccuracies were primarily noticeable around thin geometry and object boundaries.

The current BMA implementation focuses on CPU-side BVH traversal , with GPU and potentially NPU acceleration representing avenues for further development. The researchers also identify high-resolution rendering, including 8K gaming, as a potential application .


Interestingly, BMA could theoretically complement several recent ray tracing advancements we've covered, including AMD's RT-MLAS technology , NVIDIA's RTX Mega Geometry technology , and Microsoft's latest DirectX Raytracing enhancements . While these technologies primarily address the computational and memory overhead associated with constructing, updating, and managing acceleration structures for increasingly complex ray-traced geometry, BMA tackles a complementary bottleneck: the computational cost of traversing these structures .

Combining more efficient acceleration structures with intelligent traversal algorithms could help alleviate multiple ray tracing bottlenecks simultaneously.

While BMA's performance benefits in actual games remain unproven, the research provides another encouraging example of how algorithmic innovations could make computationally demanding path-traced visuals more accessible on future gaming hardware.

News Source: MDPI – Computers

  • 21-40%: Questionable - Some concerns remain

Intel's Razor Lake-AX SoCs could feature impressive graphics performance with up to 32 Xe3P GPU cores.

Intel Goes Big on Razor Lake-AX SoCs With Up To 32 Xe3P GPU Cores, Reportedly Comparable To NVIDIA's Laptop-Class 5070 Ti

Well, a lot of information on the Intel Razor Lake-AX SoCs seems to be appearing at the moment. We just covered the first visual shots of the chip itself and the configurations of the MoP & MoB parts.

Now, we have new information on the preliminary performance targets with respect to the GPU. As we know, Intel's Razor Lake-AX SoCs will come in 16- and 32 Core iGPU configurations, each based on the newest Xe3P graphics architecture. The first outing of this architecture is expected in the coming year as the Intel D-Series Workstation/AI GPUs, formerly codenamed Crescent Island. The Crescent Island chips also pack 32 Xe3P cores but operate at much higher TDPs (up to 350 watts on air-cooled models.

Since Razor Lake-AX is a complete SoC that shares its available TDP headroom with the CPU, GPU, IO, and memory (MoP variants), the iGPU will not run at the same potential as the workstation model, which also benefits from better cooling solutions. But having the same number of cores means that the graphics performance will be quite good.

As per @Haze2K1 on X, who previously reported Razor Lake-AX's MoP configuration several months back, it is said that the GPU performance of this SoC will be similar to the NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti (laptop) variant.

For reference, AMD's Ryzen Halo SoCs with Radeon 8065S/8060S iGPUs offer around RTX 5060- RTX 5060 Ti levels of GPU performance, while RTX Spark sits slightly ahead, matching the higher-end RTX 5070 (laptop). The RTX 5070 Ti laptop is anywhere around 20-30% faster than a laptop RTX 5070 so a decent performance bump right there.

This will be Intel's fastest iGPU on the market in terms of performance, even if it ends up matching an RTX 5070 laptop. But at the same time, we have to remember the timeline for when Razor Lake-AX is supposed to launch.

An early 2028 release means that Razor Lake-AX SoCs will have to compete with AMD's Medusa Halo with upgraded RDNA 5 iGPUs and NVIDIA's RTX Spark with upgraded Rubin configurations. NVIDIA has laid out its Vera Rubin Spark chip with LPDDR6 memory for 2028, and the same is true for Medusa Halo which will also support the newer LPDDR6 standard . Intel will be sticking with LPDDR5X for now.

Intel is also working on its Serpent Lake SoCs , which will feature an NVIDIA RTX GPU tile alongside its own x86 CPU architecture. That will be another chip that will be interesting to see. Razor Lake-AX SoCs will pack as much as 192 GB of memory on MoB variants , and boosted LPDDR5X memory can provide a nice bandwidth boost if coupled with a 256-bit memory controller, similar to Ryzen AI Halo, but LPDDR6 will provide a bigger lift in that department too, and bandwidth is mostly what these hefty iGPUs are lacking in the current generation.

Besides gaming, Intel is promising some big numbers with its Xe3P architecture in AI, as demoed with Crescent Island , so if those come along and win against Razor Lake-AX, then Intel will be in a very decent position with its Razor Lake-AX. With that said, these are just preliminary estimates, and we can see a lot of changes down the road, as the launch of AX is still more than a year away.

item.title: Intel Lists Raptor Lake-S NEXT In Its Own Windows Zero Copy Driver Documentation, Putting The Refreshed LGA 1700 Desktop Family On Record
item.description:
Intel appears to be preparing support for the upcoming Raptor Lake-S NEXT PV, as spotted on the official website.

New Intel Driver Documentation Explicitly Mentions Raptor Lake-S NEXT Alongside Bartlett lake-S Platform Phases

Multiple reports have indicated that Intel is preparing for a new Raptor Lake NEXT processor series, which vendors like GIGABYTE also confirmed indirectly recently . Intel has now quietly confirmed that such a processor series does exist ahead of the launch, and it's called "Raptor Lake-S NEXT", confirming the rumored family name, and also indicating that it's a desktop processor family aimed at the LGA 1700 platform.

The latest documentation shown for the Windows Zero Copy version lists support for Bartlett Lake-S Hybrid MR4, 12P MR2 , and Raptor Lake-S NEXT PV . The most interesting mention here is the Raptor Lake-S NEXT PV, and while Intel hasn't provided any detailed explanation of this, its appearance in a virtualization driver clearly indicates that Intel is working on the refreshed Raptor Lake series.

The driver is designed for virtual machine environments, and not for regular desktop use. It's based on Microsoft's Windows Indirect Display Driver model and uses a zero-copy design to transfer display frames between a Windows guest and a Linux QEMU host. According to Intel, it's required for features such as SR-IOV and KVM Multi-OS, and it also supports multi-monitor configurations.

That said, Bartlett Lake-S's mention is also interesting here. The processor family includes configurations with up to 12 P-cores and was launched for the embedded segment, even though modders later enabled support on the consumer LGA 1700 platform through workarounds. We have recently reported that MSI's Z690 and Z790 now offer support for these chips with the latest BIOS , which is a big development as well.

News Sources: @momomo_us , Intel

item.title: Elon Musk Struggles To Get Chips As Tesla’s First AI5 Chips Will Reportedly Go To Optimus Humanoid Robots, With Scarce TSMC Capacity Allocated To Microsoft And Google
item.description:
Tesla's next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) computing chip, the AI5, is unlikely to enter mass shipping in 2027, says a report from the Taiwanese media. The AI5 is slated to be Tesla's latest AI chip, and recent statements from Elon Musk have shared that the firm will use it primarily for the Optimus humanoid robot. The report suggests that Tesla's AI5 design partner, Global Unichip Corporation (GUC), is allocating limited manufacturing capacity from TSMC to products from Microsoft and Google due to higher profitability.

Microsoft & Google's Chips Win Over Tesla's AI5 In Being Able To Secure Limited TSMC Chip Production Capacity, Says Report

Tight production capacity isn't the only struggle that the AI5 chip has faced. Early in October, Musk shared that T esla was cutting the memory used by the chip to 96GB from 144GB. Musk's comments came amid the ongoing historic shortage in the global memory market, which has led to surging prices and scarce chips.

Now, a China Times report outlines that Tesla might also face tight production capacity for the AI5 chip as well. The firm shares that Tesla's AI5 design partner, GUC, is allocating the production capacity it has secured from TSMC to products from Microsoft and Google.

According to the details, while GUC's production quota from TSMC has increased for the N3 manufacturing process technology family, it is still insufficient to cater to the demand of all of its customers. Consequently, the report suggests that the firm will first allocate the production capacity to cloud service provider chips. These chips include Google's Axiom chip lineup and Microsoft's products.

The Axiom chips are Google's custom chips that rely on Arm design rules. Crucially, they are also part of the firm's TPU AI chips and serve as processors. For Microsoft, the firm currently provides the Maia custom AI chips to join Google in creating alternatives to NVIDIA's pricey products.

China Times' sources suggest that profit is the primary motive behind the allocation, as the cloud service providers have stable order visibility and strong gross profit margins. Consequently, the AI5 will not be mass-produced in 2027, especially since the AI5 quota is insufficient to meet the demand of Tesla's electric vehicles.

As a result, the supply chain expects that the first batch of the AI5 chips will be for the Optimus humanoid robots. After accumulating production experience, Tesla's cars can procure sufficient AI5 chips in 2028, says the report, which falls in line with Musk's recent remarks about the AI5 being booked for the Optimus robot.

item.title: ASRock Taichi AQUA 360 LCD AIO Launches With Dual Pumps And G1/4-inch Expansion Ports To Extend Cooling To GPUs
item.description:
ASRock reveals its new flagship Taichi AQUA 360 LCD AIO that combines a transparent, ARGB-lit coolant channel with dual pumps.

ASRock Debuts Taichi AQUA 360 LCD AIO With a Detachable 3.4-inch LCD and Dual Pumps, Backed With a 6-Year Warranty

Popular hardware maker ASRock has debuted its first Taichi series AIO cooler with the launch of Taichi AQUA 360 LCD, which now sits at the top of the tier list. The company has previously introduced several AIOs under the Challenger and Pro series, but with the introduction of its first Taichi series AIO, ASRock is aiming for a more premium user experience.

ASRock says its new Taichi AQUA 360 LCD brings flexibility to setups, allowing users to customize their own loop. The cooler is inspired by Taichi's philosophy of "infinite" potential and uses the white/silver color scheme for a sleek and premium look. AQUA 360 LCD uses a transparent section in its aluminum water block, which includes an integrated flow indicator.

The water block uses ARGB lighting that follows the coolant path, making the circulation visible. As coolant passes through the channel, it spins an internal impeller, which gives a visual indication to users that the liquid is circulating. So, the Taichi AQUA 360 LCD looks closer to a custom liquid-cooling setup than a conventional closed-loop AIO.

However, ASRock is providing users with two ways to configure the pump block. While users can use the transparent water-channel cover, they are also allowed to attach a magnetic 3.4-inch LCD. This display can show real-time system information such as hardware metrics, images, and animated GIFs through ASRock's Polychrome software.

The dual-pump configuration is also interesting, as the second pump can continue circulating the coolant even if one pump stops working. The AIO comes with a buzzer module that will also alert the user about the failure, and with both pumps operating, ASRock claims the cooler can deliver twice the coolant flow rate.

As for its radiator, it measures 38 mm and is a high-density one that comes with radiator fans with liquid crystal polymer blades and dual ball bearings. Also, ASRock has included G1/4-inch expansion ports for extending the cooling loop to additional components such as a GPU, which is rare on conventional AIOs.

ASRock hasn't disclosed the availability and pricing details for Taichi AQUA 360 LCD yet.

item.title: NVIDIA DLSS 5 Costs Red Dead Redemption 2 31% of Its 4K Performance, Yet It Almost Turns the Game Into A Movie With Natural Lighting
item.description:
In the past few weeks, we have seen plenty of examples of how NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering can significantly improve a game's visuals, regardless of the aesthetic employed. Although we have also seen examples of how games with stylized visuals such as Astral Chain and Mario Kart World work well with Neural Rendering , games such as Rockstar Games' Red Dead Redemption 2 continue to benefit the most from it, as a single pass with a modded implementation delivers such natural lighting that the game almost turns into a movie, making the performance hit well worth it.

A new comparison video shared by MxBenchmarkPC on YouTube compares the game running without NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering , with a single pass, and with a double pass.

Although the performance hit is considerable at all resolutions, with the game's frame rate taking a 31% hit at 4K resolution with DLSS 4.5 in Performance mode for a single pass, and 41% with a double pass, on an RTX 5080 , there's no denying that a single pass of Neural Rendering works wonders for lighting, shadows, and reflections, cleaning up haze and deepening contact shadows all while preserving the general feel of the vanilla game. In contrast, a double pass of NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering not only tanks performance considerably, often bringing it below 60 FPS , but also doesn't deliver the best results, as the game visuals become much darker, crushing shadow details almost as if a heavy vignette effect is applied.

The same applies to character models, as a single pass of NVIDIA DLSS 5 delivers significantly better results than a double pass, which makes characters feel unnatural and very different from how they are supposed to look.

As Red Dead Redemption 2 hasn't received official NVIDIA DLSS 5 support yet, an official implementation could have even better results, much as official ray tracing compared to the recent mod. At this time, we have no indication if this will ever happen, as only four games officially support Neural Rendering , the last of them being Where Winds Meet , which received support earlier this week.

Some unique features of the TCO27QXB include its Delta E <2 accuracy for precise colors, pixel clean technology to prevent OLED burn-in, an ergonomic design with RGB LEDs, KVM Switch, & ASRock's Low Blue Light technology.

ASRock Taichi TCO27QXB OLED Gaming Monitor: First Look and Aesthetics

The ASRock TCO27QXB comes in a large cardboard package, which is to be expected since this is a 27" gaming monitor. The front side has a picture of the monitor itself along with its model number, its size, and its maximum resolution. The back lists a few specs, but not much. The features are also mentioned in the bottom right corner.

Opening the package, you are first met with the accessories, which include the feet, the stand, the power adaptor (180W), several USB cables, and a set of HDMI / DP cables.

The full list of accessories includes an HDMI v2.1 cable and a DP v2.1 cable, both of which measure 1.5m and 1.8m, respectively.

Underneath this foam packaging is another foam container that houses the monitor itself along with the stand. ASRock has paid extra attention to securing the monitor in a foam package to avoid any damage during shipping.

The stand attaches to the feet with relative ease. All you need to do is flip the metal lever, attach the stand to the mounting bracket, and rotate the lever until it's secured. This is a fairly simple process, and getting the whole monitor ready will hardly take more than 5 minutes.

The stand looks futuristic. The monitor installation on the stand is also super easy, with a simple lock press holding the entire thing in place.

You can press the same lock to remove the panel from the stand.

The ASRock TCO27QXB is a stylish and modern 27" OLED panel. It looks great in terms of ergonomics. It has a more angular and slimmer design than the 4K QD-OLED Taichi model.

The heatsink and the vast majority of the components lie within an exterior shell on the back, while the panel is on the front and has a very thin profile.

On the back of this compartment, you can spot several exhaust vents, which are used to dissipate heat from the monitor chassis. There's also a large "Taichi" logo on the back.

That's mostly about it as far as the exterior design of the monitor is concerned.

When you fire up the gaming monitor, you can see two LED zones on the back, providing a unique aesthetic to the overall design. The illumination looks very nice in darkly lit environments.

ASRock has done a great job with its OLED design. For the ergonomic perfectionists out there, the ASRock TCO27QXB comes with several modes, allowing users to swivel (45° ~ 45°), Tilt (-5° ~ 15°), and adjust the height by up to 130mm. The monitor also supports a 100 x 100 mm VESA mounting.

The ports on the backside include 2 HDMI 2.1, 2 DP 2.1, 3 USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-A, 1 USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-B, 1 USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-C (DP / PD 65W), 1 headphone out, and two speakers, each capable of 3W. The monitor also has two buttons on the back, one to access the OSD and the other to Power On/Off.

ASRock Taichi TCO27QXB OLED Gaming Monitor: OSD

Coming to the OSD, in Standby mode, the monitor gives you the option to select from the type of output you have it plugged in with. The options include HDMI 1, HDMI 2,& and the two DP ports.

The main OSD gives you the option to select between various settings, listed in their own specific tabs, while also providing details of which mode is currently enabled at the top. It also shows the navigation buttons, making it easy for users to access the different menus.

The first settings to go through are the input selection, which lets you select between the five individual inputs: HDMI1, HDMI2, DisplayPort1, DisplayPort2, and the USB Type-C port. The USB Type-C port can be alternated between the input and a 65W power delivery output.

Next up, we have ASRock's "Image Setup" panel, which lists several modes. The TCO27QXB is set to the "Standard" mode by default. Other modes include sRGB, FPS Game, RTS Game, MOBA Game, Movie, Internet, and custom profiles. As you can tell, ASRock has modes specific to the game type, which is great to see. The sRGB mode is the go-to mode as it provides great color and brightness levels, but that's just my personal opinion.

The picture mode is the most meaty configuration tab in the OSD. It lets users adjust the brightness, set to 90% in the standard image mode, contrast, aspect ratio, sharpness levels, Dark Boost, Peak Brightness, Color temperature, 6-axis color, color space, RGB range, and Low Blue Light. The Dark Boost slider can be moved down to increase the level of darks, while increasing it essentially reduces the darks. Color Space can be switched between sRGB, Adobe RGB, DCI-P3, BT-2020, and Normal mode (set by default).

The Gaming menu lets you pick between various Aim assist technologies, along with setting up AMD FreeSync Tech, BFI, Dark Boost, DSC, a simulated size, aspect ratio, and lighting control.

The Audio panel lets you change the volume of the onboard speakers. You can also mute the speakers entirely. The last "System" menu has a host of accessibility options such as changing the Language of the OSD, Resolution, PIP/PBP, OLED Care, Lightning, Information, USB-Update, OSD Timeout, Transparency for the menu, LED Indicator Control, Auto Power Off, Time Shutdown, ECO Mode, DP 1.1, Auto Source, DDC / CI, DSC, and the option to reset all settings.

ASRock's latest OLED care solution includes Pixel Clear, which runs automatically after 4 hours of use. This can also be adjusted to manual mode which allows users to run Pixel Clear whenever the feel fit (up to 16 hours of usage). The tech will resume if interrupted, so you aren't limited in PC use when it's running. The "Logo Auto Dimming" mode will also dim the brightness levels of static logos on the screen, further preventing OLED burn-in. Besides that, there are Pixel Refresh, Pixel Shift, Static Image Dimming, and Taskbar Dimming options too.

ASRock Taichi TCO27QXB OLED Gaming Monitor: Display and Performance

Coming to the display aspects and performance, particularly in gaming, the ASRock TCO27QXB is a reasonable yet premium 27" monitor for anyone with capable hardware to drive 1440p gaming and content at a fast 540Hz refresh rate.

As I have said before, 27" & 32" are the best fit for gamers who want a great gaming experience, whether it be AAA titles or eSports games. Sure, smaller 24/21" monitors still have demand for users with limited space or those who want to carry their monitors to competitive events where you are required to bring along your own setups.

The ASRock TCO27QXB also offers great sRGB color accuracy with solid white accuracy and a peak measured brightness of over 300 nits. It comes with a decent set of calibrated modes with good color space coverage, while the response time is superb at 0.03ms.

OLED in itself will be a major game-changer for you if you are coming from an IPS, VA, or standard LCD panel. I've been using several QD-OLED monitors over the past few months, and they are a game-changer.

Additionally, the low blue light feature reduces strain on the eyes, making going through content over longer periods better.

Gaming on the monitor is wonderful, with support for FreeSync Premium Pro, which provides tear-free gaming, along with Dark Boost, which elevates the visuals to the next level.

The monitor is a great fit for the large majority of eSports gamers who will find themselves immersed in the fantastic visuals offered by the WOLED screen, while running multi-frame generation technologies like DLSS 6x modes will provide enough boost to run close to the monitor's maximum refresh rate. At 1080p, you can boost the monitor's refresh rate further up to 720Hz.

ASRock Taichi TCO27QXB OLED Monitor: Conclusion

ASRock's recent Taichi offerings leave a very positive impression. The TCO27QXB comes with solid build quality, a fantastic OLED experience, and some really fast refresh rates. The flat-panel design is great for gaming, media, and office tasks, and ASRock's low blue light technology helps reduce strain on your eyes when viewing for longer periods or gaming through hours of multiplayer sessions.

While the refresh rates are high, you'll really need some powerful hardware to even get close to the monitor's max potential. Sure, eSports titles will reach an FPS good enough to match that, but graphics-intensive titles will need to get support from multi-frame generation modes. Another thing that ASRock has done with its new Taichi OLED series is going all-in with proper DP 2.1 and HDMI 2.1 ports instead of relying on DP 1.4, which many modern monitors still pack.

Brightness levels are elevated, and HDR TrueBlack 500 really pushes for enhanced viewing experiences on the TCO27QXB. Overall, the Taichi TCO27QXB from ASRock is a great OLED monitor designed for high-end gamers who want to upgrade their existing 27" monitors to the next best thing. It offers amazing visuals, a strong set of IO features, and really fast refresh rates, elevating your PC to new heights.

Things I liked about the ASRock TCO27QXB OLED Monitor:

  • Solid QHD + WOLED Design
  • Dual mode refresh: 540Hz @ QHD / 720Hz @ FHD
  • Very low input lag, great response time, and superb motion clarity
  • Black levels handled very well ; Dark Boost tech works great
  • Solid Color Accuracy

  • IO Overload, Lots of USB ports

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Can Hit Stable 40 FPS on PlayStation 5 With Unlocked Framerate Mod, Yet High Temperatures Risk Damaging The System
item.description:
If you are following the PlayStation 5 jailbreak and modding scene, you are probably already aware that an unofficial Grand Theft Auto VI patch that can only run on jailbroken systems unlocks the game's framerate (like an Xbox Series X Quick Resume glitch does), pushing it beyond the vanilla 30 FPS cap. Early tests only confirmed that the game cannot hit a stable 60 FPS even on PlayStation 5 Pro , but another revealed how stable 40 FPS could have been within reach with a resolution compromise and if there was any way to keep the system running cooler.

Reddit user gama224 conducted a very interesting test which focused on achieving 40 FPS , revealing that by dropping rendering resolution, the 40 FPS goal was definitely possible, with 15% to 30% improvement across the board.

  • 50% render: dense area: 27-30 -> 35-40 [fps] | water area: 30 -> 45-50 [fps]
  • 60% render: dense area: 27-30 -> 30-35 [fps] | water area: 30 -> 40 [fps]
  • 55% render is the sweet spot, getting 40 fps avg (35-45) consistently and feeling smooth throughout the city.

As Rockstar Games clearly did not want to compromise the Grand Theft Auto VI's graphical fidelity and simulation elements, these tests further validate the developer's statements about choosing a 30 FPS cap across all formats.

However, there's another clear reason why the developer made its choice: the system's temperatures. According to the Reddit user, the system ran extremely hot during the tests, reaching 90°C or higher, forcing them to cap the temperature at 85°C with another homebrew app.

Considering how many users are experiencing overheating issues , it's evident that Rockstar Games took everything into account when deciding on the 30 FPS cap in Grand Theft Auto VI . Thankfully, the first taste of the 60 FPS experience that will come with the official PC port is not too far off, as unofficial ports based on the Xbox Series X version are making incredible progress, already pushing above 30 FPS and even implementing multiplayer .

item.title: Intel’s Four-Year-Old Gaudi Chips Deliver 60% Higher Decode Throughput Than NVIDIA’s H100 in Qwen3.5-27B, As AI Software Optimizations Unlock Full Potential
item.description:
Intel's older Gaudi chips are now faster than NVIDIA's H100 thanks to AI-based optimizations that bring 9.4x token throughput per dollar.

AI Optimizations Manage To Boost Intel Gaudi Chips By Up To 3.21x In Inference Benchmarks

Intel launched its Gaudi2 accelerators in 2022 , and while they were not able to match the rivals in initial benchmarks, they did offer better value. Despite the better value proposition, Gaudi hasn't seen a huge adoption; NVIDIA/AMD options have been the go-to for the majority of training and inference use cases.

Now, four years later, Intel's Gaudi accelerators have been boosted to outperform NVIDIA's H100, a chip it lagged behind during the initial launch. The boost comes through optimizations made by Standard Kernel who have been generating high-performance systems software to "unlock peak performance across all kinds of AI hardware".

For Gaudi 2, Standard Kernel made a range of optimizations that are listed below. The result is that the same chip now manages to offer 3.21x higher cached-prefill throughput, & 2.84x higher decode throughput, all coming through software optimizations alone.

  • Reduce prefill padding: use finer 128-token buckets instead of larger padded blocks. This reduces wasted computation and allows more requests to fit within the scheduling budget without splitting them.
  • Speed up prefill attention: process cached prefixes separately from causal suffixes to avoid unnecessary masking. Use batched matrix operations, larger cache-aligned K/V tiles, and more efficient softmax normalization.
  • Speed up GDN prefill: replace expensive 128×128 matrix inversions with smaller blocked inversions, accelerated by a custom TPC kernel. Reuse cached tensors and eliminate redundant forward passes.
  • Reduce GDN computation and memory traffic: use FP16 for intermediate tensors while keeping numerically sensitive operations in FP32. Normalize Q/K before head expansion and batch-independent matrix operations.
  • Optimize normalization and convolution: replace manual RMSNorm reductions and causal convolution with faster implementations, preserving the original numerical behavior and state handling.
  • Reuse shared K/V during decode: gather shared prefix data once instead of separately for each request, and maintain packed buffers for new tokens to avoid repeated data movement.
  • Reduce GDN decode state traffic: keep recurrent state in dense buffers across decode steps instead of repeatedly reading and writing the cache. Write back only when necessary.
  • Fuse decode operations: combine convolution, activation, Q/K/V extraction, and normalization into a single TPC kernel. Preserve recurrent state correctly across graph replay.

Using the same Qwen 3.5-27B model, Standard Kernel compared the optimized Intel Gaudi2 chip against NVIDIA's H100 80 GB PCIe solution. The Gaudi chip offered 60% higher throughput in the decode section and 8% higher prefill throughput than the H100.

We compared a single Gaudi2 with a single NVIDIA H100 80 GB PCIe on the following workload:

  • Model: Qwen3.5-27B-FP8
  • Concurrency: 16 requests
  • Input length: 70,000 tokens per request
  • Shared prefix: 95%

The Gaudi 2 chip does pack 96 GB of VRAM but operates at a slower 2.45 TB/s bandwidth versus the 3.35 TB/s bandwidth of the Hopper chip. We know that AI models love higher bandwidth, and despite Hopper having a 37% lead here, its hardware still lags behind a software-optimized Gaudi.

Rental costs are also on the rise as demand for compute swells across the industry. We have seen how NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper, and Blackwell rental prices continue to jump upwards. The Gaudi 2 chip, with the software optimizations, offers more performance than the H100 at 17% of its hourly rental cost, which translates to 9.4x more tokens/$.

We found Gaudi2 available to rent for $0.60/hour, compared with $3.50/hour for H100. That’s nearly a 6x difference in hourly cost. On our benchmark, the optimized Gaudi2 not only outperforms H100 in throughput, but does so at a fraction of the hourly rental cost.

While these results are fantastic for Gaudi, Intel has since abandoned its Gaudi roadmap, and the Shores lineup, which was meant to see Falcon Shores , remains in limbo. The company is working on its Xe3P-powered Crescent Island family , which will be its next major inference accelerator, and Jaguar Shores was intended for launch next year, but so far, the company has no info to share on that. For now, Crescent Island seems to be the only confirmed product family that will carry Intel's AI GPU roadmap forward.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Modded Multiplayer Runs at 25 to 30 FPS on the Unofficial PC Port, With Two Jason Duvals Sharing the Same Leonida
item.description:
Modders appear to have somehow gotten Grand Theft Auto VI multiplayer working as part of the efforts on the unofficial PC port .

The claim comes from TeK (TeKGameR / @TeKGameR950) , a French C# developer and the founder of HyTeKGames , a one-man studio seemingly active since 2011. Tek's GitHub repository calls his main project " HModding ," a universal modding platform for various games, including a work-in-progress universal dedicated server.

The repository shows the following projects:

  • Raft Mod Loader / RaftModding : the mod loader and community for Redbeet Interactive's 2022 survival game Raft, which is his best-known work.
  • Green Hell Modding : a similar community for Green Hell.
  • HModLoader : a mod loader for Unity games, on both Mono and IL2CPP.
  • HDedicatedServer : dedicated server software, still in progress.
  • Dedicated server hosting for Raft and Schedule I.

TeK's GitHub does not include his work on Grand Theft Auto VI, which is clearly still private. However, in a video shared a few hours ago on X , he shows working multiplayer, with two player characters (specifically two Jason Duval characters) and vehicles together in the same world, with proximity voice chat.

According to PortWatch (the website tracking all PC port efforts), TeK's version is a private fork of CGBJ's, the VIctory and XCL build that averages 25 fps in single-player, and appears to run between 25 and 30 frames per second.

One of the Grand Theft Auto VI multiplayer videos that have since emerged briefly shows a menu that labels the game mode as " Freeroam ". Furthermore, the menu allows the player to teleport around the map and spawn vehicles . This suggests it has been implemented by TeK, rather than something made by Rockstar and unlocked by the modder, as Rockstar certainly wouldn't want players teleporting around or spawning vehicles at will in their official multiplayer.

On that note, the developer still hasn't said anything about the multiplayer . There's speculation that it might be released alongside the PC version sometime next year, but it is just that, speculation. For now, Rockstar is keeping the focus entirely on the single player game.

In other Rockstar Games news, workers at the Grand Theft Auto VI developer have voted against union recognition (75% versus 25%) in the United Kingdom . This means management won't be required to hold regular meetings with union reps; however, the Rockstar Game Working Union (RGWU) is taking this as a mere setback, promising to put in the work to persuade the other employees in the future.

item.title: Intel Razor Lake-AX Targets Early 2028 Launch: MoP Chips With Up To 28 CPU, 32 GPU Cores & 96 GB Memory While MoB Expected To Scale Up To 52 Cores & 192 GB Memory
item.description:
New information on Intel's Razor Lake-AX SoCs, which target an early 2028 launch, has been shared, pointing out the MoP & MoB packages.

Intel Razor Lake-AX SoCs To Come In MoB & MoP Flavors: Premium Chips Scaling Up To 52 CPU Cores, 32 GPU Cores & 192 GB Memory

Yesterday, we got our first look at an early sample of Intel's Razor Lake-AX ( previously Nova Lake-AX ) chip. The sample showed us what most Razor Lake-AX chips would look like, featuring an on-package memory layout. Now, new information has been shared by Jaykihn that further details the Razor Lake-AX platform.

As per the insider, Intel's Razor Lake-AX will come in two product lines: MoP and MoB. The one we saw yesterday was an MoP design, or "Memory On-Package". This layout will feature up to four memory sites supporting up to 96 GB of LPDDR5X configurations using Micron 24 GB memory ICs. Based on availability, Intel might also leverage 16 GB modules for up to 64 GB of memory.

The Razor Lake-AX MoP products will come in an 8+16+4 core configuration on the compute tile. The cores will use the Coyote Cove P-Core architecture and Arctic Wolf E-Core architecture. These architectures are carried over from the Nova Lake family, as Razor Lake-AX is a rebadging of sorts, while the Razor Lake-S/HX families will adopt the newer Griffin Cove P-Core and Golden Eagle E-Core architectures.

Intel will also offer MoP products in a 4+8+4 core configuration, so that gives us either 28 cores or 16 cores. For the iGPU, Intel's Razor Lake-AX will come in 16 and 32 Xe3P core configurations. The MoP lineup will be leveraged by more compact form factors where size and efficiency matter the most.

Now Razor Lake-AX will also come in a MoB family, or Memory on-motherboard. These chips will use the standard chip layout with the SoC and memory featured separately on the mainboard & not in a closely packaged configuration such as the MoP offerings.

Since MoB designs will have more room on the motherboard to expand their memory footprint, they are expected to scale up to 192 GB (or 128 GB depending on availability of memory). For the CPU, Intel is said to be evaluating a dual compute tile variant of Razor Lake-AX MoB chips, which will push the core count up to 52 cores (8+16 x2 + 4), while retaining the same 32-core Xe3P iGPU.

In terms of launch, Intel is expected to launch its first Razor Lake-AX chips by early 2028 . The 12 Xe3P Desktop CPUs are also expected to launch in a similar timeframe. Commenting on the Razor Lake-S family, the insider states that we won't see them earlier and has put forward a late 2H 28 release timeframe.

Recently, it was disclosed that Intel was preparing a 12-core P-core-only option for its Razor Lake-S family, which is now said to feature 120 MB of total bLLC on a single compute tile that measures around 140mm2.

Intel Razor Lake-S will be the second desktop family on the LGA 1954 platform, with Nova Lake-S being the first. The same platform will also feature support for future Hammer Lake CPUs . Razor Lake-AX will target laptops and Mini PCs, while Titan Lake will be mobile-only, similar to Panther Lake.

item.title: AMD RDNA 5 “GFX13” GPUs Get Initial Linux 7.5 Support, With GC 13, GMC 13 Memory Controller, SDMA 8 And DCN 6 Display Code Added
item.description:
The latest AMD kernel graphics and compute driver updates are being added to Linux 7.5, which adds support for RDNA 5 GPUs & its DCN6 engine.

Next-Gen RDNA 5 "GFX13" GPU Support Is Being Cooked Up For Linux 7.5 With DCN6 Bringing Some Major Display Updates

While new client GPU news has been slow throughout the year due to the ongoing memory crisis, it looks like AMD has been silently preparing for its next-generation consumer family, RDNA 5 or GFX13.

We recently covered the latest Linux kernel patches adding significant code changes aimed at supporting the next-generation GPUs, and now, the new driver changes are being added into DRM-next ahead of the Linux 7.5 merge window, as reported by Phoronix .
